question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of A&E attendances in England in September 2026 (all A&E types, including minor injury units and walk-in centres), as reported in NHS England's monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics.

target.what: Total number of A&E attendances (all A&E types, including major A&E departments, single-specialty A&E, minor injury units and walk-in centres) in England during September 2026, as reported in NHS England's monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics (count of attendances, not unique
target.publisher: NHS England (A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions monthly statistics)
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-08 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist yet; must be forecast from prior months, seasonality and trends. Working interpretation: all A&E types combined (type 1 major, type 2 single-specialty, type 3 minor injury/walk-in/other), total attenda

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 attendances will follow the level and seasonal pattern of recent Septembers and the most recent published months (through mid-2026); a trend-plus-seasonal-factor extrapolation from the latest actual monthly totals gives the central estimate.

methods.rationale: Anchors on the most recent published monthly total (July 2026, p16) and applies a post-summer seasonal change factor. Shared dependency: relies on July 2026 being representative of the 2026 level; failure mode is an unusual September surge or dip.

methods.label: m2

p46.role: England total A&E attendances, all types, September 2025

methods.rationale: Same-month prior-year anchor (September 2025, p46) with a YoY growth factor grounded in recent 2026 growth (p19). Shared dependency with m1 on the 2026 trend; failure mode is a break in the growth trend.

methods.label: m3

p58.role: England average daily A&E attendances, June 2026

a3.role: September 2026 vs June 2026 daily-rate change factor

methods.rationale: Bottom-up from the June 2026 record daily rate (p58) scaled to 30 September days and adjusted for the post-June seasonal change. Shared dependency on the 2026 level; failure mode is a daily-rate shift between June and September.

methods.label: m4
methods.rationale: Naive carry-forward of the most recent September (2025, p46). Provides a low-growth baseline; ignores the 2026 upward trend, so it likely understates but anchors the lower end.

kept.name: September 2026 vs July 2026 total attendance change factor
kept.rationale: September typically runs slightly below the summer peak month; 2025 September (2.31m) was below the 2025 summer level, and 2026 July (p16) is a record. A modest decline of ~3% with wide uncertainty reflects month-to-month variation and trend.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 follows the usual post-summer dip relative to July.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 exceeds July 2026 or falls far below.

kept.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 YoY growth factor
kept.rationale: Recent YoY growth: July 2026 +3.3% (p19), September 2025 ~+7% (p50), September 2024 ~+4% (p1 vs p31). A ~3.5% growth is consistent with the moderating 2026 trend.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 YoY growth is near the recent 2026 monthly growth rate.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp acceleration or reversal in 2026 attendance growth.

kept.name: September 2026 vs June 2026 daily-rate change factor
kept.rationale: June 2026 daily rate 81,264 (p58) is a record; September typically slightly lower than the June peak. A ~2% decline with wide range.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 daily rate is close to but slightly below the June 2026 record.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 daily rate exceeds June 2026 or falls far below.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
